Lesson 1 · The assembly plan

Merge in the order the layers point

Build week · the trap

  • A new repo and an empty src/the autocomplete rewritten from memory, and worse
  • Deploy on Fridaythe first time production meets your env vars
  • Tests “later”so the gate never gets built

Assembly week

  • Branch the capstone stage from mainmerge bottom-up: utils → domain → ui → features → app
  • Deploy on day onean empty shell on a real URL, then every merge ships
  • Green after every mergea red test points at the last merge and nothing else
Before writing anything from scratch this week, ask which branch it already lives on. Usually the answer is one you wrote.

Lesson 2 · Three checkpoints

Auth is three checks. Only one is security.

The session lives in an httpOnly cookie, so it survives a refresh and script on the page can't read it. Middleware turns a missing cookie into a fast redirect. The server decides.

Middleware can only say “probably”. The server, at the moment it reads the data, is the one place that can say “no” — so that is where the check lives.
MODULE 12 · VIDEO 2
06 / 18
Lesson 2 · The gate sits next to the data

Check the session where the data is read

// data/session.server.ts — below features, so every feature may import it
import 'server-only';

export const verifySession = cache(async () => {
  const session = await decrypt((await cookies()).get('session')?.value);
  if (!session) redirect('/login');   // no session, no data
  return session;
});

// features/applications/api/applications.server.ts
export async function getMyApplications() {
  const { userId } = await verifySession(); // the check travels with the data
  return api.applications.listFor(userId);
}
Don't stop at the layout. A layout doesn't re-render on client-side navigation, so a check there can be skipped. A check inside the function that reads the data can't — and a new page can't forget it.

Lesson 2 · End to end means the unhappy paths

Six auth paths, each with a test

PathExpectedProved by
Signed out, open /dashboardRedirect to /login?next=/dashboardPlaywright, no cookie
Sign in from that redirectBack on /dashboard — and next must be a same-site path, or it's an open redirectPlaywright, plus a unit test that rejects next=https://…
Refresh on /dashboardStill signed in; no token in localStoragePlaywright reload
Session expires mid-taskThe next action sends you to sign in; nothing half-savedPlaywright, cookie cleared mid-test
Sign out, press BackCookie gone; no private data from the cachePlaywright
Dashboard in a search enginenoindex on every private routeAn assertion on the response

Lesson 3 · The decision record

An ADR fits on one screen

docs/adr/004-server-state.md

# ADR-004 · Server state lives in Query

Status    accepted
Context   Listings, filters and applications
          all come from the API; a hand-made
          store copied cache + loading flags.
Decision  Query owns server state, the URL
          owns filters, useState the rest.
Cost      one more dependency; query keys
          become an API to keep stable.
Rejected  Redux Toolkit: it solves client
          state we don't have.

The rules that keep ADRs read

  • One decision per filenumbered, never renumbered
  • Fits on one screenif it scrolls, it's two decisions
  • Always name the rejected optionthat line is your interview answer
  • Never edit an accepted onesupersede it with a new ADR that links back
Five to seven are enough for Rasmi: rendering per route, where server state lives, where the session lives, no component library, what earns an E2E test.

Lesson 3 · The five-minute README

Five minutes, spent in order

A reviewer opens the repo with five minutes to spare. The README decides what they see in each one.

Test it on someone who has never seen the repo: hand them the README, start a five-minute timer, then ask what they would push back on.

Lesson 3 · Deploy, and the gate that keeps it green

Every push goes through the same gate

Deploy on day one

Connect the repo to the host before the first merge. An empty shell on a real URL finds the build and env-var problems while they're small. Every PR then gets its own preview URL.

Protect main

Required status checks, no direct pushes, no “merge anyway”. If main goes red, fixing it is the only work that lands next.

Lesson 3 · The accessibility pass

A scanner finds some. You find the rest.

Automated · in CI

  • axe on every route, in Playwrightzero violations is a required check
  • Tokens checked for contrast oncethe module 7 palette passes WCAG AA
  • Roles asserted in component testsTesting Library queries by role, so a lost role fails

Manual · a scripted run

  • Keyboard only: search → filter → applyfocus always visible, never lost
  • Screen reader on combobox and modaloptions announced, focus returns on close
  • 200% zoom, then 320px wideno sideways scroll, nothing clipped
  • Reduced motion switched ontoasts and transitions respect it
Write the manual run into the README as a dated checklist. “Accessible” is a claim; a dated checklist is evidence.

Lesson 3 · The performance pass

Defend a number, its method, its commit

MetricBudgetMeasured howEnforced where
LCP≤ 2.5 sListings page, throttled mid-range mobile in the lab; p75 in the field once there's trafficThe budget step in CI
INP≤ 200 msTyping in the search box, toggling a filter on a long listA Playwright trace; field data later
CLS≤ 0.1Cold load, fonts and company logos uncachedThe budget step in CI
JS on the listings routeYour numberBundle analysis of the production build — and the ADR that set the numberA size check in CI
“It's fast” loses the argument. “Listings LCP went from before to after on throttled mobile, in commit abc123” wins it — keep that sentence, with your real numbers, in the README.

Lesson 4 · Capstone review

The senior checklist

AreaYou can showThe question you must answer
ProductThe live URL, signed out and signed in“What happens if I open the dashboard with no session?”
BoundariesLayers point down; no feature imports another“Where would a saved-jobs feature go, and what may it import?”
Typesstrict, schemas at every boundary, no stray any“What checks this API response at runtime?”
StateServer state in Query, filters in the URL“Why isn't this in a global store?”
UIThe keyboard path; combobox and modal contracts“Where does focus go when the modal closes?”
QualityGreen gate: types, lint, unit, e2e, budget“Which test catches a broken redirect?”
StoryThe five-minute README, the ADRs, the known gaps“What would you change with another week?”

Lesson 4 · Build

Hand in a URL, a green gate, a checklist

1 · The deployed URL

Public pages indexable, the dashboard behind auth and noindex. Linked at the top of the README.

2 · Green CI on main

Typecheck, lint, unit, e2e and the budget as required checks, all green on the commit you hand in.

3 · The checklist, answered

Every row of the senior checklist, with the file, test or ADR that answers it. Gaps listed honestly, not hidden.

Stage: module-12/capstone. Branch from main, merge the earlier stages bottom-up, merge back when the checklist is done. Then rehearse: open any file at random and explain why it exists, in under a minute.
